days.hook: I landed at dawn, woke up a friend at the base of the knock on the door, and hours later I was buying a bike in Sarajevo.
days.summary:
Belgrade was the prologue.Before there was a large bicycle stretch, the itinerary passed through the Temple of Saint Sava, the Kalemegdan fortress, the Pobednik and the small Ružica Church — where chandeliers made with cartridges, bayonets and other military pieces transform war memory into religious ornamentation.

Then came the flight to Sarajevo and a complete change of scenery: Baščaršija, Ottoman architecture and war marks still visible on the facades. But the main object of the journey was missing:the bicycles still needed to be chosen and bought there.Diogo left the Trek Bike Centar with a Trek Marlin 5; Giggio bought a Specialized at M-Bike. The photo inside the store records the moment the script stopped being just a plan and won the bikes that would cross the Balkans.
days.context:
Belgrade.The city occupies a strategic position in the meeting of the Sava and Danube rivers; the region was already occupied by the Roman Singidunum.

Sarajevo.The arrival places side by side the Ottoman heritage of Baščaršija and very recent marks of the siege of 1992–1996. The first pedal around town would only come the next morning.

Because the choice of bikes matters.This was not a trip when the bikes arrived home ready. Part of the first day was just finding suitable models, buying and starting to assemble logistics on two wheels.
story: Belgrade opened the journey before the bike entered the scene. The itinerary passed through the Temple of Saint Sava, the fortress of Kalemegdan, the Pobednik and the Ružica Church. Within the small church, chandeliers made with cartridges, bayonets and other military pieces condensed only the region’s relationship with successive wars.

When the first logistic improvisation appeared: without Serbian currency and with buses that did not accept a card, it was necessary to find a transport combination that did not depend on cash. Then came the flight to Sarajevo.

The Baščaršija marked its arrival in Bosnia, but the most important mission that night was still pending: there was no bicycle waiting ready. Diogo bought a Trek Marlin 5 on Trek Bike Centar; Giggio left M-Bike with a Specialized. Choosing the bikes there was part of the script itself — the equipment that would sustain the rest of the journey.
The day ended with Bosnian food — sirnica and kaftas — and bicycles finally resolved. The first pedal by Sarajevo would be for the next morning.
days.practical: Don't just count on credit cards in local transport. If the trip starts by buying a bike, book the first night for position adjustment, luggage compartment and tools.
days.food: Sirnica + kaftas. In Bosnia, burek is the version with meat; with cheese, the name is sirnica.

Baščaršija
The ancient Ottoman nucleus of Sarajevo marked its arrival in Bosnia. The next day, the first pedal would start there.
Choice of bicycles
The trip didn't have its own bikes yet. Diogo bought a Trek Marlin 5 on Trek Bike Centar and Giggio a Specialized in M-Bike — a practical stage that also became part of the story.

days.hook: 32.7 km for the city, a war tunnel, a border that is not a frontier and one of the most beautiful train paths in the Balkans.
days.summary:
The first pedal began in Sarajevo's Ottoman heart.Baščaršija is the former bazaar of the city and, in the center of the square, Sebilj — the kiosk-shaped fountain that became one of Sarajevo's symbols. The tradition of this type of public source comes from the Ottoman period; the original source of the square was from the 18th century and the current structure is from the late 19th century. From there bicycles began to sew places that, seen only as a list, seem to have no relation with each other.

From the source we go to theLatin Bridge, next to the point where Archduke Francisco Ferdinando and Sophie were murdered in 1914, and to theSarajevo Roses: marks of mortar impacts preserved on the pavement and filled with red to remind civilians killed during the siege. Then came theTunnel of Hope, dug under the runway of the airport in 1993 to connect the besieged city to free territory.

On the way back we enteredThisčno Sarajevo, already at Republika Srpska. It was not an international frontier: we continued in Bosnia and Herzegovina, but symbols, plates and alphabet changed quickly enough to make the post-war political architecture visible. After fixing Guillermo's trunk, the pedal by Sarajevo ended up in the station. The bicycles got on the train to Mostar whole — one of the easiest and most beautiful logistical decisions on the trip. The wagon followed the mountains from Bosnia to Herzegovina; already in Mostar, the night ended before the illuminated Stari Most.
days.context:
A city in layers.Baščaršija and Sebilj help to see the Ottoman Sarajevo; the Latin Bridge places the city at the heart of European history in 1914; Sarajevo Roses and Tunnel of Hope bring the 1992–1996 siege to the street range.

This in Sarajevo.Bosnia and Herzegovina is formed by internal political entities. By pedaling to Istočno Sarajevo, the trip entered Republika Srpska without leaving the country — so the feeling of “no border”.

Mustar.The Stari Most was built in the 16th century, destroyed during the war of the 1990s and rebuilt. Today the area of the historic bridge is UNESCO World Heritage Site.
story: The first pedal of the trip began in Baščaršija, the ancient Ottoman bazaar of Sarajevo. In the center of the square is Sebilj, the kiosk-shaped fountain that has become a symbol of the city. The tradition of this type of public source comes from the Ottoman period; the current structure is from the late 19th century. It was not just a beautiful spot to start pedaling: it was a way of entering the city's history by the place where trade, religion and everyday life met.

From Baščaršija we follow to the Latin Bridge. The bridge is discreet, but next to it was one of the best known episodes of the 20th century: on June 28, 1914, Gavrilo Princip murdered Archduke Francisco Ferdinando and his wife Sophie. Soon after came the Sarajevo Roses — scars left by mortar explosions on the pavement during the siege of the city, some filled with red as memorials.

The Tunnel of Hope put the war on another scale. Excavated in 1993 under the runway of the airport, the tunnel was about 800 meters long and connected to Sarajevo besieged to free territory. People, food, medicines, cables and other supplies passed by. Visiting the place helps to understand why the siege still appears so clearly in urban memory.

On the way back, the bike entered Istočno Sarajevo. There was no international border: it was still Bosnia and Herzegovina. But that area belongs to Republika Srpska, one of the country's internal entities, and this quickly appears on flags, symbols and the most frequent use of the Cyrillic alphabet. It was one of the first times that geopolitics ceased to be an abstract explanation and became a visible part of the path.

Before moving to Mostar, it was still necessary to go back to the bike shop to fix Guillermo's trunk. Then the bicycles got on the train with an ease that contrasted with many buses of the following days. The railway crossing through the mountains from Bosnia to Herzegovina has become one of the best logistical decisions of the trip.

Mostar showed up just after the day. The Stari Most, built in the 16th century, destroyed in 1993 and rebuilt after the war, was first seen with the light going down and then lit at night. The walk still passed through Spanish Square and Sniper Tower — another reminder of how, in the Balkans, beauty and war memory often occupy the same block.
days.practical: Get to the station free. On this trip, the train was much simpler to transport bicycles than several buses.
stops: Baščaršija + Sebilj

Baščaršija is the former Ottoman bazaar. Sebilj is the kiosk-shaped fountain in the center of the square and one of Sarajevo's symbols. The original source of Baščaršija was from the 18th century; the current structure is from the late 19th century. There is also the local tradition that those who drink from the sources of Sarajevo end up returning to the city.
Latin Bridge

The bridge itself is discreet; the weight is in what happened next to it. On June 28, 1914, Gavrilo Princip murdered Archduke Francisco Ferdinando and his wife Sophie — the episode that helped trigger World War I.
Sarajevo Roses

These are scars from mortar explosions preserved on the pavement. Some were filled in red at the points associated with the death of civilians during the siege, turning a physical mark of war into a memorial scattered around the city.
Tunnel of Hope

Excavated in 1993 under the runway of the airport, it was about 800 metres and was a vital connection between Sarajevo besieged and free territory. People, food, medicines, cables and other supplies passed by. Today part of the tunnel can be visited.
Thisčno Sarajevo

Crossing the eastern side was important precisely because there was no international border. It was still Bosnia and Herzegovina, but already inside the Republika Srpska; flags, writing and references changed before the bicycle.
Sarajevo–Mostar train
After the urban pedal, the train was one of the best logistical decisions of the trip: simple to board bikes and a mountain crossing that descends towards Herzegovina.
Stari Most
Mostar's stone bridge ended the day. Built in the Ottoman period, destroyed in 1993 and rebuilt, today functions as a symbol of the city and the reconstruction of the post-war period.

days.hook: Seventy miles, six punctured cameras, a motorcycle camera and a ride from a stranger who only showed up because he needed to dump the trash.
days.summary:
This was the day a small mistake became the biggest mechanical perrengue on the trip.After Blagaj and the vineyards of Herzegovina, Google Maps was set up in walking mode and took the loaded bikes to a thorny path. They got stuck in the tires and started a six-hole sequence.

Changing the camera was not enough: if the thorn remained inside the tire, the problem would come back. Then came the ascent of Svitava, the ride that took Giggio, Diogo's tire already without condition to continue and the resident who diverted dozens of kilometers to take him to Ravno. Guillermo was the one who completed the final stretch by pedaling.
days.context:
Blagaj.The source of the Buna River appears at the foot of a large karst wall and is part of one of the best known landscapes of Herzegovina.

Vineyards of Herzegovina.The route crossed a region associated with the grapes Žilavka and Blatina before entering the stretch that caused the holes.

Ćiro Trail e Ravno.Part of the route follows the former railway corridor of Herzegovina. The Stanica Ravno Hotel, installed at an old station, ended up becoming the safe haven of a chaotic day.
story: The day left Mostar by Blagaj and entered the vineyards of Herzegovina. Until then, it was exactly the kind of pedal that justified the trip: landscape, rural road and heat.

The problem began with a trivial detail. Google Maps was on foot mode and suggested a path that looked like a shortcut. For loaded bicycles, it wasn't. The stretch had thorns, and they got stuck in the tires.

Six holes came in. The repair photo represents what the count does not show: dismount wheel, look for the thorn, change camera, notice that the tire pierced again and repeat the process. The main lesson was simple — before placing another camera, you had to put your hand inside the tire and remove the cause.

Then came the ascent of Svitava. Giggio got a ride. Diogo got the tire out until a resident showed up and diverted tens of miles to take him to Ravno. Guillermo, just the least experienced of the group, finished the final stretch pedaling.
The Hotel Stanica Ravno, in an old railway station, was not just accommodation that night: it became the point where one of the most difficult days of the journey finally ended.
days.practical: Never use route “on foot” as shortcut with loaded bike. After a spike hole, review the tyre from the inside before placing another camera.
days.food: Žilavka and Blatina enter here more as part of the landscape and culture of the wine of Herzegovina.
stops: Blagaj
The source of the river Buna appears at the feet of a wall and was the great stop before the day entered the vineyards and mechanical problems.
The shortcut of the thorns
Maps was on foot. The improper road to loaded bikes left thorns stuck in the tires and fired the sequence of six holes.
Rise of Svitava
After the holes, we still had to win the climb. Mechanical wear has turned an already demanding stretch into a logistical problem.
Hotel Stanica Ravno
Old train station turned into a hotel. After the holes, the ride and the end of the pedal, it became the perfect finish point.

days.hook: Parriers, 35 degrees, a snake, an apiary used as an emergency toilet and a friend who decided to enter the trip almost without warning.
days.summary: After discovering the thorns that explained the holes the day before, the exit was delayed. Popovo Polje has brought gardening, heat and little water. Near Trebinje, the Monastery of Tvrdoš offered a break, part of an orthodox trade and finally water. In town, Leo came by surprise.
days.context: Tvrdoš maintains a long tradition of wine production. The interior of Herzegovina mixes karstic landscape, agriculture and orthodox heritage in a few kilometers.
story: Day 4 began to understand why Day 3 had been so bad: there were still thorns in the tires. Ravno's exit was delayed, and when the road finally started, the heat was already strong.

Popovo Polje was a sequence of sparrows and long stretches with little water. In a house that looked abandoned, the attempt to find a faucet ended with a snake. Shortly thereafter, a side path surrounded by bee boxes became an emergency bathroom.

Near Trebinje, the Monastery of Tvrdoš changed the rhythm of the day. I entered during part of an orthodox trade and finally managed to replenish water. It was the kind of stop that wasn’t just there for logistics — it helped to understand the region.
On arrival came another change of script: Leo had decided to go on the trip. He flew to Dubrovnik and took a taxi to Trebinje. From there the group would no longer be three.
days.practical: In hot rural stretch, carry more water than the map suggests. Monasteries and churches may save the day, but should not be the main supply plan.
days.food: The wine appears again as part of the identity of Herzegovina.

days.hook: The first day we'd be four riding, I took a cab.
days.summary: The fever had improved, but diarrhea continued. Giggio was sick too. The other three followed the bike and I took a taxi. Dubrovnik appeared across the mountains, already in the Adriatic.
days.context: Dubrovnik was the Republic of Ragusa, a maritime power that built wealth trading between Venice, the Christian world and the Ottoman Empire.
story: The fever had given in, but the gastroenteritis hasn't yet. The first day the four of them could ride together, the best plan was not to ride. The other three followed by bicycle; I crossed by taxi.
The contrast between Trebinje and Dubrovnik is fast and huge. On one side, mountain interior of Herzegovina. On the other, the Adriatic and one of the most famous walled cities in Europe.

I got here before and without much energy. It was enough to discover a practical rule that is worth more than a beautiful picture of Airbnb: inside the Old Town, stone and ladder can turn a “perfect” accommodation into a problem for those who carry bicycles and luggage.
The other three made a spectacular arrival along the coast with the sun setting. I conserved energy to get back on the bike the next day.
days.practical: Getting sick is no reason to prove anything on the bike. And accommodation inside Old Town may be beautiful, but little practice with luggage and bike.
days.food: Recovery day: priority was to arrive well, not turn food into script.

Coast on arrival
The three who pedaled arrived in late afternoon light. It was the kind of look that explains why adapting the script might be better than insisting on fulfilling a sick plan.

days.hook: Boat through the Adriatic, 40 miles of bike, ferry into Kotor Bay and a useless lap that saved my glasses.
days.summary: The day began with Dubrovnik and a boat to Cavtat. From there came the southern end of Croatia, the border with Montenegro, the Kamenari–Lepetane ferry and the Kotor Bay to Prčanj. The Garmin recorded 83.4 gross km because part of the displacement over the water entered the file; the really pedaled distance was approximately 68 km.
days.context: Kotor Bay looks like a fjord, but geologically it's a laugh: an ancient river valley flooded by the sea.
story: Before leaving, there was still time to meet Dubrovnik with a little more energy. Instead of making all the exit along the road, the bikes boarded a boat to Cavtat. From there the pedal really started.

The path crossed the southern tip of Croatia, crossed the Montenegro border and ended within the closed geography of Kotor Bay. In Kamenari, another stretch on the water: the ferry to Lepetane. Then more bike bordering the bay to Prčanj.

At night, dinner was at Capasanta Seafood Restaurant. On the way out, I thought I forgot the watch cord and came back alone. The cable was in his pocket. The return only made sense because the glasses — those yes — had stayed in the restaurant.

It is also a good example of why GPS numbers need context: Garmin's raw file marks 83.4 km, but boat and ferry entered the register. For those who want to repeat the step, the useful number is approximately 68 km effectively pedaled.
days.practical: Take out boats and ferries when interpreting a GPS file. And bring a good light: many days end after sunset.
days.food: Capasanta Seafood Restaurant. The owner was married to a Brazilian woman.
stops: Dubrovnik early
Before leaving, the city could be seen more calmly and with fewer crowds.
Boat to Cavtat
Instead of just using the road, the bikes boarded a boat through the Adriatic. It was transportation, but also part of the experience.
Kamenari → Lepetane
The ferry crosses the Strait of Kotor Bay and shortens the route. In Garmin, however, this crossing entered the archive and inflated the raw distance.
Kotor Bay
The closing of the day was pedaling through the water to Prčanj. The bay looks like a fjord, but geologically it's a laugh.

days.hook: The day I stopped crossing cities and just rode because the place was too beautiful to leave.
days.summary: Second day in Kotor. Old Town in the morning; in the afternoon, pedal the west bank of the bay passing by Muo, Prčanj and Stoliv. Our Lady of the Rocks appeared in the middle of the water and, in Verige, the small Church of Our Lady of the Angels became tiny before a huge cruise ship.
days.context: Kotor spent centuries linked to Venice. The name Verige means “currents”; the strait played a defensive role and there are reports of the use of currents to block enemy ships.
story: We stayed a second day in Kotor. That alone changed the journey: there was no other hotel to reach or luggage to carry. In the morning, Old Town. In the afternoon, Giggio and I left with the light bikes along the west bank of the bay.

Muo, Prčanj and Stoliv came in sequence, always with water on one side and the mountain closing the horizon on the other. We enter the water and follow until we see Our Lady of the Rocks — the artificial island in front of Perast.

Later, in Verige, the scene that remained in memory was another. We stopped at the little Church of Our Lady of Angels just as a huge cruise ship crossed the strait. The church and ship are not the same stop as Our Lady of the Rocks: they are two different points of the day.
On the way back, Leo joined the pedal. There was still fish soup in Capasanta and dinner at Trattoria Karampana. It wasn't the biggest pedal on the trip; it was one of the best.
days.practical: Kotor deserves at least two nights. Make a pedal without luggage: the experience changes completely. And Old Town is better sooner or at night, off the cruise peak.
days.food: Fish soup at Capasanta and dinner at Trattoria Karampana.
stops: Old Town of Kotor
Walled city with strong Venetian heritage. It's worth it sooner or later when the cruise movement goes down.
West bank of the bay
Muo, Prčanj and Stoliv form the best stretch to ride without haste and on that day without luggage.
Our Lady of the Rocks
Artificial island in front of Perast. It was seen during the pedal by the bay and should not be confused with the small church of Our Lady of Angels, later in Verige.
Verige + Our Lady of Angels
In the Strait of Verige, the small church became tiny when a large cruise ship crossed the neck. It was one of the strongest scenes of the day.

days.hook: The ticket cost €7. Driver wanted $20 a bike. And that was just the beginning.
days.summary: A bus won the ascent from Kotor to Cetinje. From there came about 34 km down towards Lake Skadar, a shortcut that turned closed trail, the Virpazar–Bar train and another 27 km of bike to Ulcinj.
days.context: Cetinje was the former royal capital of Montenegro. Lake Skadar is the largest lake in the Balkans and extends between Montenegro and Albania.
story: Using transportation was part of the design of the trip. On leaving Kotor, the bus was used to buy time and legs: the ticket to Cetinje cost €7, but the driver wanted €20 per bike.

From Cetinje began one of the lighter and funniest stretches: about 34 km down towards Lake Skadar, by rural roads with apples and blackberries along the way. Until a new “tail” turns closed trail and forces a turn.
In Virpazar, the train to Bar was simple: the bikes entered whole and at no extra cost. The only problem was getting down a station first. The train crew themselves put us back.
From Bar there were still about 27 km to Ulcinj. The stage ended at the Continental Hotel and Lungo Mare.
days.practical: In balconies, the price of the bike may depend on the driver. Ask before you board. And a “tail” on the map does not mean it is pedalable.
days.food: Dinner at the Lungo Mare, already in Ulcinj.
stops: Cetinje
Former royal capital of Montenegro. The bus was used to win the climb there and preserve energy for the most interesting stretch.
Down to Lake Skadar
About 34 km by rural roads, with apples and blackberries on the way and a feeling quite different from the coast.
Virpazar → Train bar
The bikes went in whole and at no extra cost. After several unpredictable buses, the train was almost a logistical relief.
Ulcinj
The arrival came already at night, ending a day that mixed bus, pedal, wrong trail and train.

days.hook: 46 km, heavy rain, a border on which the bicycle was faster than the cars and the arrival in the most cycling city of Albania.
days.summary: The rain pressed on the way and Leo and I took shelter in an abandoned structure. At the Sukobin–Muriqan border, the bikes passed quickly while the cars were lining up. In Shkodër, the end of the day was dedicated to solving the logistics of Lake Koman.
days.context: Shkodër is one of the most important historical cities in northern Albania and also one of the most associated with the daily use of the bicycle.
story: We left Ulcinj towards Albania with rain. When it really hit, Leo and I found an abandoned structure on the side of the road and we waited there.
The Sukobin–Muriqan border was a small bicycle victory: while the cars formed a long line, the bikes passed quickly. On the other side began Albania.

Shkodër seemed made to receive cyclists because the bike is already part of the local daily life. Before looking for the apartment, we went to Hotel Rozafa to understand where the transport to Lake Koman would come from the next day.
At night, Fisi brought Albanian food and kosi tavë. At the time of paying came another practical lesson: card was no guarantee. Leo had to cash out.
days.practical: In Albania, have cash. Confirm on the eve the exact point of transport to Koman. On rainy day, light cover and lights need to be accessible.
days.food: Fisi, with Albanian food and kosi tavë. The restaurant didn't take a card.
stops: Sukobin–Muriqan
At the Montenegro–Albania border, the bicycles passed while the cars were lining up. A rare moment when riding bikes simplified bureaucracy.
Shkodër
City where the bike is part of local routine. The arrival matched the spirit of the journey.
Hotel Rozafa
More than lodging, it became a logistic reference to find out where the transport to Koman Lake would come from.
Fisi
Albanian food dinner with kosi tavë and a practical souvenir: card was no guarantee.

days.hook: Bus, ferry by Lake Koman, Albanian Alps, Kosovo and two pedals on the same day.
days.summary: The bus left the Hotel Rozafa with the bikes inside and took to Koman. The ferry was one of the great hits of the trip. Then came Fierzë, Bajram Curri, a bus to Kosovo, Gjakovë and another 35 km of bike to Prizren.
days.context: Prizren has a strong Ottoman heritage and central importance for Albanian history: there arose the League of Prizren in 1878.
story: Day 10 began with the least romantic part of a spectacular landscape: placing four bicycles on a bus and getting to Koman on time.

The ferry through Koman Lake became one of the great moments of the journey. Walls, narrow water between mountains and the feeling of being too far from an obvious script. In Fierzë, the bikes returned to the asphalt to Bajram Curri.
We ran away thinking the bus would leave without us. When we arrived, we found out it was almost an hour away. The wait became isotonic and beer under a tree. Then the bus crossed to Kosovo.

We went down in Gjakovë and still were about 35 km to Prizren. The entrance to the city by bicycle was one of those that justify combining transportation with pedal: the bus bought time for the final part to still happen on two wheels.
At night, everyone recommended Beska. It was a good reminder that local unanimity can also err: food and service were among the disappointments of the journey.
days.practical: Koman requires combined logistics: transfer + ferry + next connection. Bus can accept bike, but don't treat it as collateral.
days.food: Isotonic and beers while the bus was not arriving; at night, Beska was the unanimous recommendation that did not work: food and service disappointed.
stops: Lake Koman
Artificial reservoir that occupies an extremely narrow valley between mountains. The ferry crossing was one of the most impressive sights of the trip.
Fierzë → Bajram Curri
Short drill in distance, but with enough climb to turn the bus clock into pressure.
Gjakovë → Prizren
After the bus to Kosovo, there was still about 35 km of pedal. The choice to use transportation bought time to reach Prizren on two wheels.
Prizren
City of strong Ottoman heritage and central to Albanian history. At night, Beska's unanimous recommendation turned out to be one of the gastronomic disappointments.

days.hook: 94 km, a frontier, a blocked path, Matka almost in the dark, a leaking tire and the most “fake-old” capital of the trip.
days.summary: A bus to Shtime jumped the big initial climb. From there began the pedal until Skopje. The detour to Matka brought blocked path, loose trunk, aid of a hardware and arrival at the end of the light. My tire lost air until Skopje.
days.context: The Skopje 2014 project put neoclassical facades, museums and monumental statues in the center. The contest of symbols linked to Alexander was part of the conflict of identity with Greece which ended in the Prespa Agreement.
story: The day began in Prizren and used a short bus to Shtime to avoid the great initial ascent. The idea was to save the legs for one of the largest pedals on the trip — 94.4 km registered to Skopje.

Near Matka, Guillermo and I separated from the other two to make the detour. A path that looked like a military or restricted area forced him to return. Shortly thereafter, his trunk began to break loose.

A small hardware solved the problem in a way that became a memory of the journey: the man gave us screws and refused to charge. Matka appeared already at the end of the light, too late to deserve the visit that the place asked for.
On the way out, my tire started losing air slowly. The solution was pragmatic: fill, pedal, fill again and continue until Skopje.
At night came the contrast: the monumental center looks ancient, but much is the result of the project Skopje 2014. The best outcome was the Old City House, where the best sheep on the trip appeared.
days.practical: Matka deserves half an hour, not half an hour. Take extra screws or clamps to the trunk and keep the pump accessible if the tire starts to lose air.
days.food: Old City House: Best sheep on the trip.
stops: Prizren → Shtime by bus
The short bus stretch eliminated an uninteresting climb and left power for the 94.4 km registered in the rest of the day.
Matka Canyon
The Treska River passes between limestone walls. The arrival happened too late for boat or kayak — and it became clear that Matka deserved half a day.
Lock on the way
When Guillermo's trunk started to drop, a man supplied bolts and refused to charge. A little meeting that became part of the memory of the stage.
Skopje
The first impression was monumental. Only then did it become clear that much of the “old” appearance of the center came from the Skopje project 2014.

days.hook: Three bikes, a frustrated bus attempt at 11:00, a last ram and the arrival in one of the most beautiful cities on the trip.
days.summary: The morning mission was to find a suitcase or box to dispatch the bikes. Three stores and nothing. The 11 o’clock bus filled; the following options were vans that did not fit four bicycles. A larger bus solved the afternoon and Ohrid still appeared with light.
days.context: Ohrid was one of the great religious and cultural centers of the medieval Slavic world. The tradition of the “365 churches” explains the nickname Jerusalem of the Balkans.
story: The morning in Skopje had a concrete mission: to find a solution to dispatch the bike on the return flight. Three bikes later, there was no suitcase or box.
The 11:00 bus to Ohrid was already full. The following alternatives were vans — and four bicycles completely changed the equation. We managed to secure a bigger bus for later.

Leo stayed at the bus station for a work meeting. Giggio and I took advantage of the wait to go back to the Old City House and repeat the lamb that had ended the night before. We still cycle through the center, passing the house-memorial of Mother Teresa and the new Church of Saint Constantine and Saint Helena.
The bus arrived in Ohrid before the end of the light. Santa Sofia, the waterfront and lake made the city enter immediately among the most beautiful of the journey. Dinner ended at Vkusno.
days.practical: Van is hardly ever good news with four bikes. If you need a bike bag or a box for the flight, settle it before the last day.
days.food: Giggio and I went back to the Old City House to repeat the sheep. At night, dinner at the Vkusno in Ohrid.
stops: Bike Skopje
The search for a suitcase for the bicycle ended up becoming an urban tour of three bicycles and the monumental center.
Mother Teresa Memorial House
Mother Teresa was born in Skopje in 1910. The present memorial is not the house where he was born; it is near the church where he was baptized.
Church of Saint Constantine and Saint Helena
Inside it seems very ancient, but the present temple is recent — another example of how Skopje mixes historical appearance and contemporary construction.
Ohrid
The arrival with still light immediately revealed why the city would be one of the favourites: lake, churches and a historic center that descends to the water.

days.hook: A saint whose “heart” I swear I heard, smoked duck, wine and a van that forced us to return to the bike.
days.summary: Burek and pistachio croissant opened the day. The shore of Lake Ohrid led to Sveti Naum, Sveta Petka and the Albanian border. In Pogradec, smoked duck and wine. After almost two hours of waiting, the van did not take the bikes — then the day went back to pedaling.
days.context: Part of Lake Prespa's water crosses the Galičica mountain underground and reappears in the springs of Sveti Naum. Prrenjas is in a corridor used from the ancient Via Egnatia.
story: Day 13 began at Wake & Bake with meat burek and pistachio croissant. The departure of Ohrid was light, accompanying one of the oldest lakes in Europe.

Leo and Guillermo passed through Sveti Nahum without realizing that the monastery was there. I went in; Giggio, who was behind, went in too. In the tomb of San Naum there is a tradition of touching the ear and hearing beats. I heard.
Shortly afterwards, Sveta Petka showed another image difficult to forget: crystalline water running inside the small chapel. The Sveti Naum–Tushemisht border put the journey back in Albania.

In Pogradec, the Rose and Tymour stop was long: smoked duck — one of Guillermo’s favorite foods — and wine. At the bus station, almost two hours waiting for a van ended in a simple answer: the bicycles did not fit.
The result was to return to the saddle. More ascent, more miles and the sunset on the way to Prrenjas, where the lodging needed to be resolved on site.
days.practical: Just consider the bus taken care of after the bike is in. Sveti Naum deserves a real stop, not just a quick photo.
days.food: Wake & Bake: meat burek + pistachio croissant. In Pogradec, Rosa and Tymour: smoked duck and wine.
stops: Lake Ohrid Margin
The beginning of the day was one of the most beautiful and quiet pedals of the trip, accompanying the water to Sveti Naum.
Monastery of Sveti Naum
In the tomb of the saint there is a tradition of touching the ear and hearing beats. In Diogo's experiment, he listened.
Sveta Petka
Small chapel where crystal clear water runs from the inside — an easy to miss stop if the trip turns into only mileage.
Rose and Tymour
In Pogradec, smoked duck and wine became a long pause. Then the van that didn't take the bikes returned the group to the road.

days.hook: 65 km, two buses for four bikes, cardboard boxes, a race tennis and a dawn dismounting the same bike three times.
days.summary: The last big pedal followed the Shkumbin valley to Elbasan. Only two bikes fit on the first bus to Tirana. In the capital, three cardboard boxes came from Absolute Bike & Rent and the rest of the day became parting logistics.
days.context: Shkumbin is an approximate division between traditional areas of the gheg and tosk dialects. Tirana became capital only in 1920 and concentrates Italian, communist and contemporary layers.
story: The last big pedal followed the Shkumbin valley to Elbasan. It was Day 14 and the trip could still create a new problem: four bicycles and a bus that only accepted two.

Leo and I got the first one. Giggio and Guillermo had to wait for the following. In Tirana, I went straight to Absolute Bike & Rent, with whom I had spoken before, and got three cardboard boxes. Leo had taken his own bike trunk.

Lunch at Capital Restaurant Piceri took place while the accommodation was booked. Then I bought Adidas Adiero Evo SL for the marathon, Guillermo bought jamón and wine and made the last dinner together.

I was the only one who would fly that morning. At the airport point, the promised “bus” appeared as a van. The bicycle was dismantled, reassembled in the airport parking lot and disassembled again at the terminal to finally be dispatched.
It was a coherent ending with the 14 days: the bicycle was the thread of the journey; improvising transportation was part of the route.
days.practical: Cardboard box works very well if the company accepts. Confirm shuttle size, time and vehicle type — and have a plan B. As a group, be ready to share bikes on different buses.
days.food: Capital Restaurant Piceri during the search for accommodation. Then last dinner of the group; Guillermo still bought jamón and wine.
stops: Shkumbin Valley
The last big pedal followed the valley to Elbasan, in a corridor used from the ancient Via Egnatia.
Elbasan
The city grew around a fortress and still maintains life within the walls: streets, houses, church, mosque and restaurants.
Bus to Tirana
Only two bikes fit on the first bus. The group ended the trip as they had traveled several times: adapting logistics in real time.
Absolute Bike & Rent
After three unsolved bikes in Skopje, three cardboard boxes in Tirana finally solved how to get the bikes on the plane.
